title: A linked pull request suggests the feature's status
subtitle: Mock-ups for GitHub issue #1800, on invented data (alertly/web). Light frames as pictures; open any HTML frame with ?theme=dark.

decisions.name: Linking a pull request
decisions.question: How is a pull request linked to a feature, and how is it shown in the panel and on rows?
decisions.common: Every proposal uses the one feature panel, shows each pull request's state as Open, Merged or Closed, keeps the feature's code with its name, and turns a commenter's link into a proposal.

proposals.name: Field with a picker
proposals.what: The feature panel gets a Pull requests field under Status. Each linked pull request shows its state (Open, Merged, Closed) and its title; one whose title names the feature's code links by itself, marked with an (i). "Link a pull request" opens a small search of the connected repo's recent pull requests; Link adds one. Each Priorities row gets one chip: "Open", "1 of 3 merged" or "Merged". A commenter's link becomes a proposal.
proposals.plus: One field, one chip per row; linking works for features with or without a code; the panel stays the one place to change it.
proposals.cost: 3 clicks + a few keys per link; today there is no way to link a pull request at all.

frames.caption: Priorities at rest: each row with linked pull requests shows one chip, e.g. Weekly alert digest "1 of 2 merged".
The owner opens Weekly alert digest and clicks Link a pull request: a search of the repo's recent pull requests opens in the field.
They type "unsub": only #503 Unsubscribe link in the digest footer is left.
They click Link: #503 joins the list as Open, and the row's chip reads "1 of 3 merged" at once. Cost: 3 clicks + 5 keys.
Many pull requests (9, long titles, one closed): the field lists them all, wrapping; the row chip still reads one line, "5 of 8 merged".
The same feature with 9 pull requests at the owner's 1512 width.
Phone: the row chip wraps under the name; the panel is the bottom sheet, the field sits under Status.

proposals.why: It is the product's own pattern (a field with Change-style actions in the one feature panel), works for features with no code, and keeps each row to one short chip however many pull requests there are.

proposals.name: Code in the title
proposals.what: No picker: a pull request links itself when its title or text names the feature's code ("F-79"). The panel lists what was found and offers "Copy F-79", with the two steps behind an (i). Rows show a small glyph with the count.
proposals.plus: Nothing to do in Oracle once the team names codes; no searching.
proposals.cost: 1 click to copy + 4 keys in GitHub per pull request; today no way to link.

frames.caption: Priorities at rest: a small glyph and count on each row with pull requests.
In the panel, the (i) beside Copy F-79 shows the two steps.
The owner clicks Copy F-79: the button shows it is copied.
Lena opens #503 with F-79 in its title: it shows in the panel by itself, marked found by its code. Cost: 1 click + 4 keys in GitHub.
A feature with no code yet (Mobile alert push, not in the Ground Truth): nothing can name it, so it shows "Needs a code first".
The same feature with no code at 1512.
Phone: the panel's bottom sheet with the found pull requests.

proposals.name: Paste a link
proposals.what: The panel's Pull requests field has a box that takes a pasted pull request link. Rows show each pull request as its own chip, "#482 Merged", two at most, then "+N".
proposals.plus: Works with any link a person already has; rows say exactly which pull request is in which state.
proposals.cost: Copy the link in GitHub, 2 clicks + paste; today no way to link.

frames.caption: Priorities at rest: up to two pull request chips per row, each with its number and state.
In the panel the owner clicks into the link box.
They paste the link to #503.
They press Enter: #503 joins the panel's list; on the row it only adds to "+1", and the name wraps. Cost: 2 clicks + paste, after copying in GitHub.
Many pull requests: the row shows two chips and "+7"; rows get busy.
The same rows at 1512.
Phone: the chips wrap onto their own line under each name.

proposals.name: Own panel section
proposals.what: Pull requests get their own section lower in the panel, grouped Open, Merged and Closed with counts. "+ Link pull requests" opens a dialog where several can be ticked at once. Rows show nothing.
proposals.plus: Links several at once; the panel's top stays as it is; rows stay calm.
proposals.cost: Scroll + 4 clicks for two links; today no way to link.

frames.caption: The panel scrolled to its Pull requests section, grouped by state; the rows behind show nothing.
The owner clicks + Link pull requests: a dialog lists the repo's recent pull requests.
They tick #503 and #502.
They click Link 2: both join the Open group. Cost: scroll + 4 clicks.
9 pull requests: the section grows long, far below the fold.
The same long section at 1512.
Phone: the section at the foot of the bottom sheet.

decisions.name: The status suggestion
decisions.question: Where does Oracle's suggested status show, and how does the owner accept or dismiss it?
decisions.common: A pull request never changes status by itself: when all of a feature's linked pull requests merge Oracle suggests Done (one opening suggests In progress), and a person accepts or dismisses; a commenter proposes. Shown with LP1 A's field and chip. The Inbox and rail counts are not redrawn in these mock-ups; built, every count moves at once.

proposals.name: Mark, panel and Inbox
proposals.what: When all of a feature's linked pull requests merge, Oracle suggests Done (an open one suggests In progress). The suggestion shows as a "✦ Done?" mark on the feature's row, as a box under Status in its panel, and as a Status row in the owner's Inbox, each with Accept and Dismiss. Acting in one place clears it everywhere. A commenter sees "Propose Done"; a viewer sees the mark only. With several pull requests it waits until the last one merges; the (i) says which.
proposals.plus: Seen wherever the person looks; same Accept and Dismiss as Oracle's date suggestions today.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks (mark, Accept); today 4 clicks in the panel, and only if someone notices.

frames.caption: Priorities at rest: Weekly alert digest shows "3 of 3 merged" and a "✦ Done?" mark.
The owner clicks the mark: the panel opens with "Oracle suggests Done" under Status, Accept and Dismiss.
The (i) says why: 3 of 3 pull requests merged, the last on Nov 23.
They click Accept: Status reads Done, the box goes, the row shows "✓ Done". Cost: 2 clicks.
The same suggestion's Status row is gone from the Inbox too; only the late feature with no pull request stays.
A commenter: the panel's box offers "Propose Done" and no Dismiss; it becomes a proposal for the decider.
The commenter's panel at 1512.
Phone: the bottom sheet with the suggestion under Status.
Detailed: the same Status row in Detailed's Inbox (the one Inbox), here at rest before any accept.

proposals.why: The rule says Oracle suggests and a person confirms; this puts the suggestion where people already work (the row, the panel, the Inbox) with the same Accept and Dismiss as Oracle's date suggestions, so nothing new to learn.

proposals.name: Inbox only
proposals.what: Suggestions land only in the Inbox, as Status rows with the change ("Planned → Oracle suggests Done"), why, Accept and Dismiss, and an "Accept all" for several. Rows and panel stay as they are.
proposals.plus: One list to clear; Accept all handles a busy week in one click.
proposals.cost: 1 click for all 4; today 4 clicks per feature.

frames.caption: The Inbox with 4 Status suggestions, Accept all 4, and one late feature with no pull request.
The (i) on Weekly alert digest lists its 3 merged pull requests.
The owner points at Accept all 4.
They click it: all 4 rows go. Cost: 1 click for 4.
A commenter: each row offers Propose, with no Accept all.
The commenter's Inbox at 1512.
Phone: each Status row stacks, actions under it.
Detailed: the 4 suggestions and Accept all 4 in Detailed's Inbox, the same list.

proposals.name: Row popover only
proposals.what: Only the Priorities row shows "✦ Done?"; clicking it opens a small popover with why, Accept and Dismiss, like the Timeline's date popover. No Inbox row.
proposals.plus: Fast for someone ranking work on Priorities.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks; today 4 clicks in the panel.

frames.caption: Priorities at rest with the "✦ Done?" mark on Weekly alert digest.
The owner clicks it: a popover says Oracle suggests Done, 3 of 3 merged, with Accept and Dismiss.
They point at Accept.
They click it: the mark goes and the row shows "✓ Done". Cost: 2 clicks.
A commenter: the popover offers Propose Done only.
The commenter's popover at 1512.
Phone: the mark under the name, its popover over the row.

decisions.name: Set-up and broken links
decisions.question: How does an owner see that GitHub is not connected or a link no longer resolves, and fix it?
decisions.common: No prose: a state chip and an (i). Inbox counts are not redrawn in these mock-ups. Connect GitHub shows only to those who may connect it; a viewer sees the state only.

proposals.name: Fix where it shows
proposals.what: Problems show in the panel's Pull requests field, where the link lives: a link that no longer resolves reads "Can't be found" (red), with Fix (Remove the link, Link another), and its row gets a "⚠ 1 link" chip. With GitHub not connected the field reads "GitHub not connected" with Connect GitHub for those who may connect it; rows show no chips.
proposals.plus: No new page or list; the fix is one click from the problem.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks (Fix, Remove); today there are no links to break.

frames.caption: The panel: #466 can't be found, in red, with Fix; the row behind shows "⚠ 1 link".
The owner clicks Fix: Remove the link and Link another.
They point at Remove the link.
They click it: #466 is gone from the field and the row's warning goes. Cost: 2 clicks.
GitHub not connected: the field says so with Connect GitHub; no row chips anywhere.
Not connected, at 1512.
Phone: the broken link and Fix in the bottom sheet.

proposals.why: It follows the rule that every problem leads to the item with the action that fixes it, in the one feature panel, without adding a page-wide banner or new Inbox noise.

proposals.name: Inbox fixes
proposals.what: Each broken link is an Inbox row ("Link broken", the feature, #466 can't be found) with Relink and Remove; a missing connection is one Inbox row with Connect GitHub.
proposals.plus: Nothing to hunt for: problems arrive with the rest of the owner's work.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks + a few keys to relink; today no links to break.

frames.caption: The Inbox: a Link broken row for #466 on Weekly alert digest, with Relink and Remove.
The owner clicks Relink: the repo search opens in the row.
They type "unsub".
They click Link on #503: the broken-link row is gone. Cost: 2 clicks + 5 keys.
GitHub not connected: one row, "4 features wait on it", with Connect GitHub.
Not connected, at 1512.
Phone: the Link broken row stacked, actions under it.
Detailed: the same Link broken row in Detailed's Inbox.

proposals.name: Strip on Priorities
proposals.what: A warning strip at the top of Priorities: "GitHub not connected" with Connect, or "1 pull request link can't be found" with Show, which lists each with Remove.
proposals.plus: Impossible to miss on the page that ranks the work.
proposals.cost: 2 clicks; today no links to break.

frames.caption: Priorities with the warning strip: 1 pull request link can't be found.
The owner clicks Show: #466 on F-79 Weekly alert digest, with Remove the link.
They point at Remove the link.
They click it: the strip goes. Cost: 2 clicks.
A viewer with GitHub not connected: the strip shows, with nothing they can do.
The viewer's strip at 1512.
Phone: the strip wraps above the list.
